sentences.text: Ruth's check rises every year, and it buys less than her first one.
sentences.spoken: Ruth's check rises every year, and it buys less than her first one.

sentences.text: At 65, she chose the smaller annuity check that rises 2 percent a year, and asked one thing: would 2 percent keep up with prices?
sentences.spoken: [curious] At sixty-five, she chose the smaller annuity check that rises two percent a year, and asked one thing: would two percent keep up with prices?

sentences.text: Her twentieth year of checks ended this August.
sentences.spoken: Her twentieth year of checks ended this August.

sentences.text: We tested that raise against every 20-year stretch of US prices since 1947, to see how often it kept its buying power, and how much it usually kept.
sentences.spoken: We tested that raise against every twenty-year stretch of U.S. prices since nineteen forty-seven, to see how often it kept its buying power, and how much it usually kept.

sentences.text: Here, keeping up means a check still buys at least what its own first check bought.
sentences.spoken: Here, keeping up means a check still buys at least what its own first check bought.

sentences.text: Ruth is an illustrative retiree, built on real US prices, and today her check falls short of that.
sentences.spoken: Ruth is an illustrative retiree, built on real U.S. prices, and today her check falls short of that.

sentences.text: This is US only, and it's history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: This is U.S. only, and it's history, not a forecast.

sentences.text: It doesn't say which check to choose.
sentences.spoken: It doesn't say which check to choose.

sentences.text: At 65, an income annuity can pay a bigger check that never changes, or a smaller check that rises by the same percentage every year.
sentences.spoken: At sixty-five, an income annuity can pay a bigger check that never changes, or a smaller check that rises by the same percentage every year.

sentences.text: How much smaller the rising check starts depends on the insurer, and this video doesn't model it.
sentences.spoken: How much smaller the rising check starts depends on the insurer, and this video doesn't model it.

sentences.text: So it can't compare the dollars both checks pay out over a lifetime.
sentences.spoken: So it can't compare the dollars both checks pay out over a lifetime.

sentences.text: What it measures is buying power: what each check can buy, compared with what its own first check bought.
sentences.spoken: What it measures is buying power: what each check can buy, compared with what its own first check bought.

sentences.text: Ruth took her first rising check in August 2006.
sentences.spoken: Ruth took her first rising check in August two thousand six.

sentences.text: Her reasoning was simple: prices go up, and her check goes up too.
sentences.spoken: Her reasoning was simple: prices go up, and her check goes up too.

sentences.text: So what does a raise of 2 percent a year add up to?
sentences.spoken: So what does a raise of two percent a year add up to?

sentences.text: After 20 raises, a check is 48.6 percent bigger than its first one.
sentences.spoken: After twenty raises, a check is forty-eight point six percent bigger than its first one.

sentences.text: Over Ruth's 20-year stretch, the consumer price index rose 64.3 percent.
sentences.spoken: Over Ruth's twenty-year stretch, the consumer price index rose sixty-four point three percent.

sentences.text: That index is a national average of what urban households pay for, from rent to medical care to gasoline, not any one person's own basket.
sentences.spoken: That index is a national average of what urban households pay for, from rent to medical care to gasoline, not any one person's own basket.

sentences.text: Her check grew, but prices grew more, so today it buys less than her first check did.
sentences.spoken: Her check grew, but prices grew more, so today it buys less than her first check did.

sentences.text: If her first check bought 10 crates of everything the index tracks, her check today buys about 9.
sentences.spoken: If her first check bought ten crates of everything the index tracks, her check today buys about nine.

sentences.text: Measured against its own first check, the bigger level check she turned down would buy about 6 in 10 today.
sentences.spoken: Measured against its own first check, the bigger level check she turned down would buy about six in ten today.

sentences.text: So the raise slowed the loss.
sentences.spoken: So the raise slowed the loss.

sentences.text: That's measured against each check's own start, and the level check started bigger, by an amount this video doesn't model.
sentences.spoken: That's measured against each check's own start, and the level check started bigger, by an amount this video doesn't model.

sentences.text: Year by year, Ruth's check bought at least what her first one did on 12 of its first 15 anniversaries.
sentences.spoken: Year by year, Ruth's check bought at least what her first one did on twelve of its first fifteen anniversaries.

sentences.text: It slipped under in a few early years, then climbed back each time.
sentences.spoken: It slipped under in a few early years, then climbed back each time.

sentences.text: In August 2021, at 80, her check still bought a little more than her first one did.
sentences.spoken: In August twenty twenty-one, at eighty, her check still bought a little more than her first one did.

sentences.text: Then, in a single year, it fell below, and it hasn't caught up since.
sentences.spoken: [serious] Then, in a single year, it fell below, and it hasn't caught up since.

sentences.text: By August 2022, it bought 94.5 percent of what her first check did.
sentences.spoken: By August twenty twenty-two, it bought ninety-four point five percent of what her first check did.

sentences.text: Measured against its own start, the level check she turned down fell that far much sooner.
sentences.spoken: Measured against its own start, the level check she turned down fell that far much sooner.

sentences.text: By year 5, it was already down to about 9 in 10.
sentences.spoken: By year five, it was already down to about nine in ten.

sentences.text: Her rising check stands there now, after 20 years.
sentences.spoken: Her rising check stands there now, after twenty years.

sentences.text: So was Ruth's stretch unusual, or is this what a 2 percent raise usually did?
sentences.spoken: So was Ruth's stretch unusual, or is this what a two percent raise usually did?

sentences.text: We took every starting month from January 1947 to August 2006, and followed prices for 20 years after each one.
sentences.spoken: We took every starting month from January nineteen forty-seven to August two thousand six, and followed prices for twenty years after each one.

sentences.text: That's 715 stretches, and Ruth's is one of them: the most recent.
sentences.spoken: That's seven hundred fifteen stretches, and Ruth's is one of them: the most recent.

sentences.text: For each one, we asked Ruth's question: did a check rising 2 percent a year still buy at least what its first check bought?
sentences.spoken: For each one, we asked Ruth's question: did a check rising two percent a year still buy at least what its first check bought?

sentences.text: Each tile here is one stretch, lined up by the month it started.
sentences.spoken: Each tile here is one stretch, lined up by the month it started.

sentences.text: It kept up in 17 of the 715.
sentences.spoken: It kept up in seventeen of the seven hundred fifteen.

sentences.text: That's about 1 in 42.
sentences.spoken: That's about one in forty-two.

sentences.text: Every one of those stretches started between September 1947 and January 1949.
sentences.spoken: Every one of those stretches started between September nineteen forty-seven and January nineteen forty-nine.

sentences.text: Since then, no starting month has kept up, including Ruth's.
sentences.spoken: Since then, no starting month has kept up, including Ruth's.

sentences.text: In the typical stretch, prices rose 3.1 percent a year.
sentences.spoken: In the typical stretch, prices rose three point one percent a year.

sentences.text: So after 20 raises, the rising check typically bought 80.7 percent of what its first check bought.
sentences.spoken: So after twenty raises, the rising check typically bought eighty point seven percent of what its first check bought.

sentences.text: In crates, the typical rising check ended with most of its 10 still lit.
sentences.spoken: In crates, the typical rising check ended with most of its ten still lit.

sentences.text: A level check, over the same stretches, typically kept 54.3 percent, about half.
sentences.spoken: A level check, over the same stretches, typically kept fifty-four point three percent, about half.

sentences.text: And typically, the level check had already sunk to where the rising check would end by about year 8.
sentences.spoken: And typically, the level check had already sunk to where the rising check would end by about year eight.

sentences.text: Again, that's buying power against each check's own start, not dollars paid.
sentences.spoken: Again, that's buying power against each check's own start, not dollars paid.

sentences.text: Even the stretches that ran through the gentler 2000s and 2010s, the years closest to Ruth's own, fell short.
sentences.spoken: Even the stretches that ran through the gentler 2000s and 2010s, the years closest to Ruth's own, fell short.

sentences.text: And over 25 years, not one stretch kept up.
sentences.spoken: And over twenty-five years, not one stretch kept up.

sentences.text: We also ran it on the index Social Security uses for its yearly raises, with about the same result; on a gentler price measure, the raise kept up more often but still fell short in most stretches.
sentences.spoken: We also ran it on the index Social Security uses for its yearly raises, with about the same result; on a gentler price measure, the raise kept up more often but still fell short in most stretches.

sentences.text: Then why did the same raise land so differently from one start to another?
sentences.spoken: Then why did the same raise land so differently from one start to another?

sentences.text: Ruth isn't the worst case, and she isn't the best.
sentences.spoken: Ruth isn't the worst case, and she isn't the best.

sentences.text: Carl, also illustrative, took the same kind of rising check in January 1966.
sentences.spoken: Carl, also illustrative, took the same kind of rising check in January nineteen sixty-six.

sentences.text: His 20 years had the fastest price rise of any stretch: 6.38 percent a year.
sentences.spoken: His twenty years had the fastest price rise of any stretch: six point three eight percent a year.

sentences.text: Like Ruth's, his first check bought a row of 10 crates.
sentences.spoken: Like Ruth's, his first check bought a row of ten crates.

sentences.text: On every one of his 20 anniversaries, his check bought less than it had the year before.
sentences.spoken: On every one of his twenty anniversaries, his check bought less than it had the year before.

sentences.text: Ruth's check climbed back in her early years; Carl's never did.
sentences.spoken: Ruth's check climbed back in her early years; Carl's never did.

sentences.text: After 20 raises, his check bought 43.1 percent of what his first check bought.
sentences.spoken: After twenty raises, his check bought forty-three point one percent of what his first check bought.

sentences.text: A level check, in his stretch, would have bought 29 percent.
sentences.spoken: A level check, in his stretch, would have bought twenty-nine percent.

sentences.text: His raise helped, and it still left him with less than half.
sentences.spoken: His raise helped, and it still left him with less than half.

sentences.text: He wasn't alone: stretches that began in the 1960s typically ended at 44.3 percent.
sentences.spoken: He wasn't alone: stretches that began in the 1960s typically ended at forty-four point three percent.

sentences.text: Edna, also illustrative, started in January 1949, the last starting month when a 2 percent raise kept up.
sentences.spoken: Edna, also illustrative, started in January nineteen forty-nine, the last starting month when a two percent raise kept up.

sentences.text: Twenty years later, her check still bought at least what her first one did.
sentences.spoken: Twenty years later, her check still bought at least what her first one did.

sentences.text: She is part of that early handful, and nobody who started after her got that answer.
sentences.spoken: She is part of that early handful, and nobody who started after her got that answer.

sentences.text: Her 20 years ended a few years into Carl's.
sentences.spoken: Her twenty years ended a few years into Carl's.

sentences.text: The same few years of prices came at the end of her stretch, with all 10 crates still lit, and at the start of his.
sentences.spoken: The same few years of prices came at the end of her stretch, with all ten crates still lit, and at the start of his.

sentences.text: And Ruth, at 85, is still losing ground.
sentences.spoken: And Ruth, at eighty-five, is still losing ground.

sentences.text: In the year to this August, prices rose 3.4 percent, more than her 2 percent raise.
sentences.spoken: In the year to this August, prices rose three point four percent, more than her two percent raise.

sentences.text: That's one year of history, not a forecast for the year after it.
sentences.spoken: That's one year of history, not a forecast for the year after it.

sentences.text: Same raise, same rule: Edna kept up, Ruth fell short late, and Carl fell far behind.
sentences.spoken: Same raise, same rule: Edna kept up, Ruth fell short late, and Carl fell far behind.

sentences.text: In crates, Edna's row ended full, Ruth's at about 9, and Carl's at about 4.
sentences.spoken: In crates, Edna's row ended full, Ruth's at about nine, and Carl's at about four.

sentences.text: What differed was the month each one started, and what prices did after that.
sentences.spoken: What differed was the month each one started, and what prices did after that.

sentences.text: So what raise did keep up, in this history?
sentences.spoken: So what raise did keep up, in this history?

sentences.text: A raise of 3 percent a year kept up in 42.4 percent of the 20-year stretches.
sentences.spoken: A raise of three percent a year kept up in forty-two point four percent of the twenty-year stretches.

sentences.text: About 3.1 percent kept up in half: that's the typical rate from before, a median of the past, not an expectation.
sentences.spoken: About three point one percent kept up in half: that's the typical rate from before, a median of the past, not an expectation.

sentences.text: Keeping up in every stretch took the rate of Carl's years.
sentences.spoken: Keeping up in every stretch took the rate of Carl's years.

sentences.text: These rates describe what prices did; this video doesn't say which check, or which raise, to choose.
sentences.spoken: These rates describe what prices did; this video doesn't say which check, or which raise, to choose.
